acceptanceCriteria: Completed-test navigation buffers are released after writing; a repeated closed-test harness shows bounded retained heap independent of suite length.
Retry replacement, second-page refusal, context close and golden-byte tests still pass.
body: Confirmed during issue #814 round-2 review, HEAD 52a09ef16d8b43723b6f4e2bfe89f031a414d052. Installed Core 1.0.0-rc.3 build407, Tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build407. navigation-events.cjs:97 stores every test state; :165-169 flush deletes only contexts, while tests retains all event arrays after output. Synthetic Node --expose-gc harness using createRecorder, one page per test, 30 closed tests with 512 unique URLs each (about 2060 bytes), serialized valid files below 4 MiB, measured +32911400 heap bytes after GC while recorder remained installed. Expected completed tests release large buffers; actual worker memory grows with all completed navigations and can exhaust memory in long suites despite individual bounds. Dispose buffers after final flush, preserving retry/multi-page refusal metadata. Reproduction used only built-ins and a disposable output directory; no source changes.

completion.reason: Fixed in #814 review round 2: navigation-events event buffers are released after each document write, and a second context closing in the same attempt withholds the document (ANL-V0-043/045). Codex round 7 PASS. Delivered in beamfall/corvint#816, merged to main at 469f260b8. Tests on go1.27.2: the batch's focused packages PASS, go vet clean, doc gates PASS, CEM check and seal PASS. full-gate (make gate) NOT_RUN (owner scoped-work preference). Evidence: sha256 of the lane build-log record at the merge commit.

title: Navigation-events producer retains completed-test event buffers for the entire worker
